brief: The bonfire never re-asks its weather. `bonfireWeather()` is consulted when the heap is lit and nothing consults it again, so a fire started in a calm dawn burns on through an afternoon gale that `isWindy()` would have refused outright; #156 re-keyed the bar onto the graded `windF` but did not add the re-ask. Make the fire a thing the weather can end — or hold, or hurry — after it is lit, so that a gale arriving over a lit bonfire is legible in the frame rather than ignored by it. Why now: Sky, light & weather is 10 iterations back, this cue (c244) has survived two manager passes, and #171's law came out of exactly this shape of bug.
successLooksLike: Over a seeded year, count fires that begin in weather `bonfireWeather()` accepts and are still burning in weather it would refuse: non-zero on HEAD (quote it), zero or bounded on the candidate. The change is visible at least once in a filmstrip of the day it fires.
avoid: PREMISE UNVERIFIED BY THIS PASS — I read it out of c244 and did not re-count it. Count it on HEAD first, and if a fire never in fact outlives its weather, say so, DELETE the cue's sentence, and let the measurement be the deliverable. Watch the edge: LAWS says attribute an edge-triggered event AT THE EDGE, because `washOut()` flips on `raining` while `wetF() > 0.22` holds it false long afterwards, and the bonfire's terms have the same shape. Do not turn this into a new weather scalar; it is a re-ask of one that exists.
